record.paper_title: Some open problems about the solutions of the delay difference equation x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/x_{n-k}^p
record.context_brief: Stability and basin of the period-two cycle
record.original_question: Let a>0 and consider x_{n+1}=a/x_n^2+1/x_{n-1} for n=0,1,..., with positive initial values. A period-two cycle for this recurrence is a nonconstant positive sequence r,s,r,s,... satisfying the recurrence. For exactly which values of a is the period-two cycle asymptotically stable, and what is its basin of attraction among positive initial conditions?

evidence.quote: When (18) holds, Eq. (16) has a periodic cycle with period two, {p, q, p, q, . . . }.
Open problem 1. ... (b) For what values of a is the periodic cycle {p, q, p, q , . . . } of Eq. (16) asymptotically stable? What is its basin of attraction?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a real parameter $a>0$ and consider the second-order rational difference equation
$$x_{n+1}=\frac{a}{x_n^{2}}+\frac{1}{x_{n-1}},\qquad n=0,1,2,\dots,$$
with positive initial conditions $x_{-1},x_0\in(0,\infty)$, so that $x_n>0$ for all $n\ge -1$.

A period-two cycle is a nonconstant solution of the form $\dots,p,q,p,q,\dots$ with $p,q>0$ and $p\ne q$; equivalently, $(p,q)$ satisfies
$$p=\frac{a}{q^{2}}+\frac{1}{p},\qquad q=\frac{a}{p^{2}}+\frac{1}{q}.$$

(i) Determine the set of values of $a>0$ for which a positive period-two cycle $\{p,q\}$ exists and is locally asymptotically stable as a 2-periodic solution of the recurrence.

(ii) For those values of $a$, describe explicitly the basin of attraction of $\{p,q\}$, i.e. the set of positive initial pairs $(x_{-1},x_0)\in(0,\infty)^2$ such that the resulting solution $(x_n)$ satisfies $\lim_{n\to\infty}x_{2n}\in\{p,q\}$ and $\lim_{n\to\infty}x_{2n+1}$ equals the other element of $\{p,q\}$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search returned general work on basins of attraction of period-two solutions of monotone/rational difference equations, but no source verifying a complete answer for this specific equation $x_{n+1}=a/x_n^2+1/x_{n-1}$. The status of the asymptotic stability and basin description of its period-two cycle could not be confirmed as resolved.

status_evidence.title: Basins of attraction of period-two solutions of monotone difference equations
status_evidence.snippet: Boundaries of basins of attraction of period-two solutions are described as global stable manifolds of neighboring saddle points for general monotone second-order difference equations.
status_evidence.claim: General framework exists for basins of period-two solutions, but no specific resolution for the given equation was found.
